title: Command dispatch completeness
description: Every command the parser declares reaches an implementation. The dispatch source MUST NOT carry a wildcard match arm, so the compiler's own exhaustiveness check decides completeness: a command added to the parser with no arm is a build failure rather than a command that exits successfully having done nothing. Discharged by the command-dispatch-completeness checker in verification support, which scans the dispatch source. Attested by the @contract scenario in features/command-dispatch.feature.
rationale: A wildcard arm is the production form of a glob that reads nothing: both report success for work never done, and a green run cannot see either. tinman replay shipped declared in the parser, advertised in the help text, accepted by the command parser and reachable by the interactive assistant, while a wildcard arm swallowed it and exited 0. The arm is what made the gap invisible; an exhaustive match would not have compiled. Banning the arm hands the obligation to rustc, which never forgets it, rather than to a reviewer who reads the enum and the dispatch in separate sittings. The token is the arrow rather than a whole arm, so a wildcard is caught whatever body follows it.
